newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol steady, expiry mutes trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol steady, expiry mutes trade.

text.p: Implied volatility of notionnel options traded on MATIF was steady on Wednesday, ahead of the expiry of August options next session, traders in Paris said.

Activity was limited, traders said, with the imminent expiry draining liquidity from the market. Also the underlying futures market is locked in a stop-go cycle which is keeping volatility on its toes, but with little firm movement.
"Notionnel is moving in steps, with periods of activity then periods of calm," said a trader at a French house in Paris. "The problem is that there appears to be no end to this."

August notionnel options on the September futures were trading at a range of volatilities between 4.8 and 4.9 percent, but traders said the imminent expiry meant levels were unreliable. More than 3,200 calls were traded at the 131.00 strike, and 900 of the 130.00 puts.
September options were at 4.40 percent for the 130.00 strike, and 4.15 percent for the 131.00 strike, little moved from Tuesday. September notionnel futures were up 0.34 at 130.94 by 1145 GMT.

A French broker said most volume was on the call side, with the September 131.00 strike racking up more than 1,700 lots, and the 132.00 and 133.00 strikes seeing volume of 1,500 and 1,000 respectively. Puts were more muted, with the 126.00 strike attracting most interest.
He said volatility was fairly valued at the moment, and there was little pressure to push it either way.
Further out December options volatility was stable at 5.6 percent.
